steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I can see how someone who's never known life outside the prison would be scared of the world.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Well, thankfully, I know how it all turned out in the end. She left with them. If I didn't know that, this is about where I'd start getting all anxious.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Isn't that great~?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: So after that was when they started preparing for the jailbreak, right?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: That's right.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: It should've been about a month and a half after Kafka was put in prison when Anthony made the decision to get out. Then, it took them about another month to come up with a concrete plan to get out of there.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Which means there was about a month and a half from the time they finished their plan till the actual jailbreak, right?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: It was four months altogether. It's not that long, but it's not that short either.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: But I guess we're finally at the part I'm interested in the most.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...What's this diagram?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Oh, I know. this is the prison's layout, right?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: That's right~ It's kinda crude, but it's got everything you need to know on there.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: The part that I'm the most curious about is how they got out.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Of course, I'm interested in the story behind the team, but this is a prison break! That's the part that keeps us all on the edge of our seats~!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You told me you wanted to understand the whole process. Is that really just because you're interested in the jailbreak?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Sure, you can think of it like that.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Fine.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: If we're going to talk about it, we might as well start from the beginning.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: First, let's take a look at the prison's design. The architects clearly learned from their experience with the nomadic cities. The prison wasn't built directly on top of the chassis.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: They built a mountain base first, like what you'd find in the real world, and then they finished the prison design on top of that.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: This is a pretty common technique these days, but, back in the day, it was ahead of its time, and it was very successful.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Now, let's set aside the prison's outside appearance for the time being.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: The prison has three floors, and each floor's structure is more or less the same.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: At the lower-left of each floor is the A-Zone. This is where the non-Infected are kept.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: To the upper-right is the B-Zone, the Infected block.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: The upper-left and lower-right corners are where the guardhouses are. That's where the jailers usually stay.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: The black monolith in the center is the C-Zone, where the most serious felons are kept.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: The area in the middle here is the underground factory. This is where the prisoners work together.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Over here is the clinic. It's also Domma's room. Next to that is the morgue.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: On the other side is the library that they built at Anthony's suggestion.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: That's more or less the prison's layout.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Mina spent a bit of time exploring, and with the basic idea figured out, they came up with a way to escape from the prison.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You can tell by looking at the layout that the C-Zone tower isn't actually built directly onto the ground.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: There is an elevator in the middle that goes to the basement. Not only that, but the tower itself can actually be lowered underground.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Ohhh? No kidding?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Yeah, these kinds of structures aren't very common. They probably designed it that way so that they can keep the inmates underground during emergencies, where they can't cause trouble.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Right, and to lower the tower, you normally need to flip the switches in two of the guardhouses at the same time.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Oh, I get it.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: The info I got after the fact did mention that the tower sank all the way to the bottom, so they probably activated the mechanism at the guardhouses, right...? Huh? Wait a minute... That doesn't make sense.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Even if they made it underground, was there a way out down there?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: First off, they didn't go to the guardhouses. They thought about it at one point.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: However, they found out the mechanisms could only lower the tower very slowly.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Anthony figured that out from a document he found in the library.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: The document was probably a design diagram left behind after the prison's construction. My assumption is no one thought about it, so they stuck it in there when Anthony suggested building a library.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Hah.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: They probably figured no one would ever need that for anything. After all, the prison was built more than twenty years ago.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: It was twenty-five years ago.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: In any case, they couldn't just wait for the tower to slowly sink to the bottom. The guards would have tried to do something, and so they abandoned this idea altogether.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Huh? But in that case...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Fortunately, they found something else on the document—

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Take a look at the top of the central tower. There's a room here, and it isn't a prison cell.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: That's the real control room of the tower, if not the whole prison.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: The control room... I see. That's where you can make the tower drop all the way to the bottom, right?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: That's right, and it's also possible to cut off the prison's electricity there to cause a commotion, however brief.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: There usually isn't anyone on that floor. You need a special elevator key to get inside. The regular keycards that the jailers carry can't access this floor.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I think I get it now. They went up to the control room, sank the tower all the way to the bottom, and cut the power off to cause a ruckus up above.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: But that still leaves us a question—

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: What happened after that.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Is there a way out underground?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: There is.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Domma provided that way out.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: She said that, going by her memory, the last morgue doctor had told her there weren't any previous designs the architects could reference when building the prison, and there were actually a few abandoned structures at the bottom of the mountain.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: And some of those led to the surface outside the prison.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: In particular, there was one fairly close to the morgue.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: It's close, but there's also a wall that's three meters thick in-between.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: So... did they dig their way through?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Yes, they dug through the wall.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: The walls themselves are made of rebar and concrete, but it's just soil outside.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Once you find a weaker section of wall and breach it, you don't need any advanced tools to dig the tunnel.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: That's what they did, they took turns digging at the clinic.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Huh? Now that you mention it, if they were going to dig a tunnel at the morgue, couldn't they have left as soon as the tunnel was done?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Have you forgotten already? Getting to the surface outside the prison isn't going to do you much good when the prison isn't stopped at a city.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: The prison also raises its security whenever it stops at a city. When that happens, the prisoners get much less free time.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Even Anthony hardly had any free time.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: They couldn't just have gone to the clinic like before.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Oh, right. Teehee, I forgot.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Right, since the prison was stopped at a city, Mina left with the construction crew before the jailbreak, so she didn't actually participate in it.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: She rendezvoused with the gang outside the prison.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Anyway, at some point in the last month and a half, they stole the key that gave them access to the control room at the top of the tower from Chief Barton.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Then, a few days before the prison was slated to make its next port call, they finished digging the tunnel and made sure it led them to the surface.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Now all the preparations were finally complete.
